channel.title: Insights - Adventure Spirit Consulting
channel.description: Expert articles on the Croatian Cybersecurity Act, the 13 measures of the Regulation, self-assessment scoring, incident reporting, ISO standards and risk management.

item.title: How the self-assessment is actually scored: the Pi and T thresholds
item.description: An explanation of the scoring system in the ZSIS evaluation framework: the minimum threshold per control, the additional average threshold per sub-measure, and why formal compliance is not enough.

item.title: Active Directory: five findings we see in almost every assessment
item.description: The most common findings in Active Directory security assessments: legacy protocols, excessive delegation, passwords in attributes, stale privileged group membership, and access to domain backups.

item.title: AI in defence: where it genuinely helps and where it just moves the problem
item.description: A realistic assessment of applying AI in cyber defence: where it delivers measurable benefit, where it creates false confidence, and which controls to put in place before adopting it.

item.title: NIST CSF 2.0 and the Govern function: a framework that finally named the board
item.description: What the Govern function brings to NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, how the six functions map to the 13 measures of the Croatian Cybersecurity Regulation, and why the framework is worth using as a common language with the board.

item.title: The AI system inventory and the asset register: why they are one list
item.description: How to extend an existing information asset register so it covers the AI Act's inventory requirements, instead of maintaining a separate register of AI systems.

item.title: What cyber insurers actually ask before they quote
item.description: Which questions recur in cyber insurance questionnaires, why premium and cover are tied to specific controls, and how to use your existing compliance evidence in the negotiation.

item.title: Prohibited practices and AI literacy: two provisions already in force
item.description: Which practices the AI Act prohibits outright, what the AI literacy obligation in Article 4 means, and how to satisfy it without building a separate training programme.

item.title: The DORA register of information: it fails on data, not on the rules
item.description: What DORA requires in the register of information on contractual arrangements with ICT service providers, why populating it stalls on data quality, and how to connect it to your existing asset and risk registers.

item.title: The AI Act: four risk levels and the question that comes first
item.description: How the EU AI Act divides systems into four risk levels, what makes a system high-risk, and why classification has to start from an inventory of the AI systems in your organisation.

item.title: A BIA that produces a usable RTO, not a number everyone ignores
item.description: How to run a business impact analysis under ISO 22301 so that RTO and RPO are usable: who supplies the data, how to avoid everything being critical, and how the BIA connects to measure 12 of the Croatian Cybersecurity Regulation.

item.title: ISO 27002:2022: 93 controls and the five attributes most people skip
item.description: What changed in ISO/IEC 27002:2022 - four themes instead of fourteen clauses, 93 controls and five attributes. How to migrate an existing Statement of Applicability without losing the evidence base.

item.title: 24 hours, 72 hours, 30 days: deadlines that run in parallel
item.description: Deadlines for reporting a significant cyber incident under the Croatian Cybersecurity Act: early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, final report within 30 days, and the parallel notification under Article 33 GDPR.

item.title: A risk register that passes review: five recurring mistakes
item.description: The most common mistakes in risk registers that surface during compliance reviews: no link to the asset inventory, risks without owners, scores without reasoning, treatment plans without deadlines, and a register that never changes.

item.title: You hold ISO 27001. How much is it worth under the Cybersecurity Act?
item.description: How much of the 13 measures of the Croatian Cybersecurity Regulation is covered by ISO/IEC 27001:2022, where the real gaps are, and how to map existing controls instead of writing new documentation.

item.title: 13 measures, 99 sub-measures, 132 controls: the anatomy of Annex II
item.description: A complete overview of the 13 cyber risk management measures from Annex II of the Croatian Cybersecurity Regulation: sub-measures per measure, what each asks for in practice, and how they connect to the control catalogue.

item.title: Entity categorisation under the Croatian Cybersecurity Act, and what follows from it
item.description: How it is determined whether you are an essential or an important entity under the Croatian Cybersecurity Act, which deadlines run from the categorisation notice, and how the duties of the two groups differ.
